extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the EU AI Act establishes two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, and quality management system plus technical documentation assessment by a notified body under Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification), providers may use internal control (Annex VI) or notified body assessment (Annex VII) depending on whether harmonised standards have been applied; Annex VII (notified body) is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements.
Substantial modifications to a high-risk AI system require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in systems designed to continue learning after being placed on the market.

Under Article 46, a market surveillance authority may, by way of derogation from Article 43 and for exceptional reasons of public security, health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets, authorise placing a high-risk AI system on the market without the standard conformity assessment, for a limited period.

Under Article 43, for the conformity assessment procedure referred to in Annex VII, the provider may generally choose any notified body, except where the high-risk AI system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or Union institutions/bodies/offices/agencies, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body.

Notified bodies may, in specified circumstances under Annex VII (4.5), be granted access to training and trained models of an AI system, including relevant parameters, to assess conformity, after other verification means have proven insufficient, subject to IP and confidentiality protections.
Article 43(5) gives the European Commission power to adopt delegated acts updating Annex VI and Annex VII procedures in light of technical progress, without need for full legislative revision.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes administrative rules for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies under the AI Act.

A Council document (ST-7322-2026-INIT) sets out codes and categories (e.g., AIP 0101, AIP 0102) corresponding to AI systems under Annex I, used to scope the designation of conformity assessment bodies notified under Article 30 of the Regulation.

A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836 / 2025/0359 (COD)) would create a new Annex XIV listing categories and corresponding types of AI systems for the Commission's NANDO notified-body information system, and would amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements.
As of October 2025, the NANDO system lists 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies under the Medical Devices Regulation framework, not specific to the AI Act.
As of late June 2026, zero notified bodies had been designated under the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) in the Commission's NANDO database, a separate but related EU product regulation.
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem specifically for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and capacity described as limited.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act in the medical devices context.

One source states that post-2026, notified bodies designated under the AI Act will begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments, intersecting with existing MDR/IVDR notified body assessments.

One news source claims that under a final text agreed in September 2026, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from 2 August 2029 rather than 2 December 2027, with the delay attributed to harmonised standards and notified bodies not being ready.

Another news source states the Annex III obligations start date was moved to 2 August 2029 following a 'second amendment of Article 113' replacing a 2 December 2027 date set by an 'AI Omnibus', and that providers will not need notified body conformity assessment for these systems until then.

A client alert dated 2026-09-29 states that EU institutions deferred application of AI Act high-risk requirements for Annex III systems to 2 August 2029, to allow time for harmonised standards and first notified body designations.
A separate source states that high-risk AI obligations under the AI Act fully apply in August 2026, which is described as the key deadline for medical device AI (SaMD) compliance.
A SaaS-focused compliance source references an August 2, 2026 deadline for issuing EU Declarations of Conformity for high-risk AI systems.
An industry compliance source (eyreACT, undated but referencing 'as of March 2026') states that an 'August 2026 deadline isn't moving' for engaging a notified body.

The original 2021 Commission proposal text and a 2022 proposal draft of Article 43 described the same two-track system (internal control vs. notified body assessment via harmonised standards or common specifications) as later adopted, indicating continuity from proposal to final law.

contradictions.claim_a: High-risk AI obligations under Annex III apply from 2 August 2029, per a 'final text agreed in September 2026' replacing the earlier 2 December 2027 date.
contradictions.claim_b: High-risk AI obligations fully apply in August 2026, described as the key deadline for medical device AI (SaMD) compliance.
contradictions.description: Sources disagree sharply on when Annex III high-risk AI obligations take effect: one (dated Sept 2026) says 2 August 2029, while another (undated) says August 2026, a three-year discrepancy that cannot both be correct; the 2026-dated sources are more likely current given later publication dates.

contradictions.claim_a: The Annex III high-risk deadline was moved to 2 August 2029, following the AI Act's final text agreed in September 2026.
contradictions.claim_b: An 'August 2026 deadline isn't moving' for engaging a notified body, implying the relevant deadline remains in 2026.
contradictions.description: One source (eyreACT, undated, referencing March 2026 conditions) insists an August 2026 deadline is fixed and not moving, while later-dated sources (Sept 2026) report the deadline was moved to August 2029; this suggests the eyreACT source is outdated relative to the September 2026 developments, but the sources directly conflict on the applicable deadline.

contradictions.claim_a: The Annex III deadline shift to 2 August 2029 resulted from a 'final text agreed in September 2026.'
contradictions.claim_b: The same shift to 2 August 2029 is described as resulting from a 'second amendment of Article 113... following the AI Omnibus,' implying a different and possibly earlier legislative mechanism/timeline for the same change.
contradictions.description: Two similarly-dated sources describe the same 2 August 2029 date but attribute it to different legislative mechanisms ('final text agreed in September 2026' vs. 'second amendment of Article 113' via an 'AI Omnibus'), leaving it unclear which characterization of the legal process is accurate.

open_issues: No official EU source (eur-lex, AI Act Service Desk, or Commission document) among those provided directly confirms the 2 August 2029 date for Annex III high-risk obligations; this claim rests solely on three undated or September 2026 news/blog sources, not an official legal text.

It remains unclear whether any notified bodies have been formally designated specifically under the EU AI Act as of the research date (2026-10-04); available sources only report on MDR/IVDR and CRA notified body designations, or state that AI Act designation was still in progress as of March/April 2026, with no source confirming any actual AI Act notified body designation.

The exact relationship between the proposed COM(2025) 836 regulation (creating Annex XIV for NANDO) and the final adopted structure of the AI Act's notified-body regime is unclear, since source 9 describes this as a proposal, not confirmed adopted law.
The specific list of notified bodies designated under Article 30 and referenced in the Council document (source 8) is not provided, only the coding scheme for scope of designation.

Sources do not clarify whether the Annex VI/Annex VII procedural framework described in Articles 43 and 16 has been formally amended since the AI Act's 2024 entry into force, despite references to a 'second amendment of Article 113' and an 'AI Omnibus' process.
No source clarifies the current (October 2026) number or identity of any AI Act-specific notified bodies, if any have since been designated between April/June 2026 and the present date.

The interplay between the conformity assessment timeline changes (2027 vs 2029) and the previously stated August 2026 deadlines for CE marking, declarations of conformity, and compliance checklists is not reconciled across sources.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes a two-track conformity assessment regime for high-risk AI systems under Article 43: internal control (Annex VI) or notified body assessment (Annex VII), with the applicable route depending on the system's category and whether harmonised standards have been applied (low-medium confidence). While the legal framework itself is reasonably well-documented, the practical infrastructure of designated notified bodies specifically for the AI Act remains largely unbuilt as of the research date, and sources sharply disagree on the timeline for when high-risk obligations actually take effect.

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two primary routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or quality management system plus technical documentation assessment by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) [powerquant.eu](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF Working Paper](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf). For Annex III point 1 systems (biometric identification), notified body assessment (Annex VII) is reportedly mandatory, while other Annex III categories may use internal control depending on standards compliance (low confidence) [Kop EU AI Act](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment). For high-risk AI systems already covered by sectoral EU product legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery) under Annex I Section A, providers must follow the relevant sectoral procedure, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai).

Substantial modifications generally trigger a new conformity assessment, with an exception for predetermined changes in continuously-learning systems (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard assessment for exceptional public security, health, or infrastructure reasons, for a limited period (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk Art. 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46). Providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU-institution use cases, where the relevant market surveillance authority itself acts as the notified body (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk Art. 43 (ga)](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43). Notified bodies may, under specified conditions, be granted access to training data and trained models when other verification proves insufficient, subject to IP protections (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7). The Commission retains power under Article 43(5) to update Annexes VI and VII via delegated acts (low confidence, single source) [FPF Working Paper](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf).

### Notified Body Designation
Administrative infrastructure for notified bodies is addressed in Article 35 (identification numbers and lists) (low confidence) [regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35), and a Council document references coding categories (e.g., AIP 0101) used to scope designations under Article 30 (medium confidence) [Council ST-7322-2026-INIT](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf). A pending Commission proposal would create a new Annex XIV for the NANDO notified-body database and amend aviation regulation 2018/1139 (medium confidence) [Council ST-15708-2025-INIT](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf). As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies—figures tied to medical devices regulation, not the AI Act specifically (high confidence) [EUR-Lex SWD(2025)1051](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051). Multiple lower-confidence sources suggest that, as of March–April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated specifically under the AI Act, with designation processes still ongoing across Member States (low confidence) [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide). # Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes a two-track conformity assessment regime for high-risk AI systems under Article 43: internal control (Annex VI) or notified body assessment (Annex VII), with the applicable route depending on the system's category and whether harmonised standards have been applied (low-medium confidence). While the legal framework itself is reasonably well-documented, the practical infrastructure of designated notified bodies specifically for the AI Act remains largely unbuilt as of the research date, and sources sharply disagree on the timeline for when high-risk obligations actually take effect.

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 of the AI Act establishes two primary routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or quality management system plus technical documentation assessment by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) [powerquant.eu](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF Working Paper](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf). For Annex III point 1 systems (biometric identification), notified body assessment (Annex VII) is reportedly mandatory, while other Annex III categories may use internal control depending on standards compliance (low confidence) [Kop EU AI Act](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment). For high-risk AI systems already covered by sectoral EU product legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery) under Annex I Section A, providers must follow the relevant sectoral procedure, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai).

Substantial modifications generally trigger a new conformity assessment, with an exception for predetermined changes in continuously-learning systems (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to derogate from standard assessment for exceptional public security, health, or infrastructure reasons, for a limited period (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk Art. 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46). Providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU-institution use cases, where the relevant market surveillance authority itself acts as the notified body (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk Art. 43 (ga)](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43). Notified bodies may, under specified conditions, be granted access to training data and trained models when other verification proves insufficient, subject to IP protections (medium confidence) [AI Act Service Desk Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7). The Commission retains power under Article 43(5) to update Annexes VI and VII via delegated acts (low confidence, single source) [FPF Working Paper](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf).

### Notified Body Designation
Administrative infrastructure for notified bodies is addressed in Article 35 (identification numbers and lists) (low confidence) [regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35), and a Council document references coding categories (e.g., AIP 0101) used to scope designations under Article 30 (medium confidence) [Council ST-7322-2026-INIT](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf). A pending Commission proposal would create a new Annex XIV for the NANDO notified-body database and amend aviation regulation 2018/1139 (medium confidence) [Council ST-15708-2025-INIT](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf). As of October 2025, NANDO listed 51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies—figures tied to medical devices regulation, not the AI Act specifically (high confidence) [EUR-Lex SWD(2025)1051](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051). Multiple lower-confidence sources suggest that, as of March–April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated specifically under the AI Act, with designation processes still ongoing across Member States (low confidence) [eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide). For comparison, zero notified bodies had been designated under the related Cyber Resilience Act by June 2026 (low confidence) [cybercertlabs.com](https://www.cybercertlabs.com/case-studies/insights-cra-notified-bodies-2026).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources conflict significantly on timelines. Three low-confidence sources dated September 2026 state Annex III high-risk obligations were deferred to 2 August 2029 [eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update), [ai-law-insights.example](https://ai-law-insights.example/2026/09/22/when-do-annex-iii-rules-apply), [tech-legal-alerts.example](https://tech-legal-alerts.example/2026-09-29-ai-act-high-risk-timeline), while other low-confidence sources insist an August 2026 deadline applies and "isn't moving" [mdxcro.com](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd), [eyreact.com](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act). The September-dated sources also disagree among themselves on the legal mechanism (a "final text" versus a "second amendment of Article 113" via an "AI Omnibus"). None of these timeline claims are confirmed by an official EU legal source, and all carry low confidence (below 0.4).

## Knowledge Gaps
No official source confirms whether any notified bodies have been formally designated specifically under the AI Act as of October 2026. The relationship between the proposed Annex XIV/COM(2025)836 framework and the final adopted notified-body structure is unresolved. The specific list of bodies designated under Article 30 remains unavailable. Whether Articles 43/16 have actually been amended (as implied by references to an "AI Omnibus" and Article 113 changes) is unconfirmed by primary legal text.
